Estimate bank weights by entropy-penalised maximum likelihood

Source: R/bank.R
fit_bank.Rd

Given candidate trajectories and the log-likelihood of every participant under each, estimates how often each candidate occurs in the population. The objective is the marginal log-likelihood of the donor measurements plus an entropy penalty, $$J_\lambda(p) = \sum_{j} \log \sum_m p_m \, p(Y_j \mid \theta_m) + \lambda H(p), \qquad H(p) = -\sum_m p_m \log p_m .$$

Usage

fit_bank(loglik, lambda = 1, start = NULL, maxit = 5000L, tol = 1e-08)

Arguments

loglik

A donor-by-candidate log-likelihood matrix, as returned by trajectory_loglik(). Donors must not include any participant who will later be scored against the resulting bank (see Details).

lambda

Entropy penalty, non-negative.

start

Optional starting weights; defaults to uniform.

maxit, tol

Optimiser controls.

Value

An object of class mbmm_bank: a list with weights, the donor-by-candidate posterior responsibility, the attained objective, lambda, and convergence information.

Details

With lambda = 0 this is the nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator on a fixed support, whose solution is extremely sparse and unstable when many near-identical trajectories compete for the same donors. The entropy term spreads weight across such near-duplicates. For lambda > 0, the entropy term is strictly concave and the maximum is unique in the relative interior of the simplex. At lambda = 0, a maximum need not be unique.

The objective is a sum over donors, not a mean. Raising lambda with a fixed donor set therefore strengthens the penalty relative to a fixed amount of data, but holding lambda fixed as donors accumulate lets the penalty become negligible.

Honesty. The bank used to score a participant must be built without that participant's measurements. Pass a disjoint donor set, or use bank_loo() to refit leaving each scored participant out in turn.

See also

bank_loo(), restrict_bank(), class_loglik()

Examples

set.seed(1)
LL <- matrix(rnorm(20 * 6), 20, 6)
b <- fit_bank(LL, lambda = 1)
round(b$weights, 3)
#> [1] 0.336 0.030 0.058 0.203 0.268 0.105
